title: The Structure of Oleate-Capped CdSe Nanocrystals Determined by DNP-Enhanced Dipolar Dephasing Solid-State NMR Spectroscopy
abstract: Semiconductor nanocrystals (NCs) are of interest due to their tunable electronic and optical properties. However, the atomic-level characterization of surface structures of NCs remains an unresolved challenge. Here, we demonstrate that rotational-echo double-resonance (REDOR) experiments can be used to determine structural models of surfaces of CdSe NCs. An atom-efficient ligand-exchange scheme is demonstrated to introduce partially 13C-enriched oleate ligands onto CdSe NCs and enable 13C-dephased REDOR experiments.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Asymmetric Total Syntheses of (+)-Asperterpenoids D and E with a Concurrent Synthesis of ent -(−)-Homoverrucosanol
abstract: The first asymmetric total syntheses of sesterterpenoids (+)-asperterpenoids D and E, together with a concurrent synthesis of diterpenoid ent-(−)-homoverrucosanol were achieved from (S)-limonene through a chiral-pool strategy featuring a common late-stage intermediate. Key transformations include a Michael addition and a highly diastereoselective Type I [5 + 2] cycloaddition, which successively establish the C-14 and C-11 methyl-bearing stereocenters with complete stereocontrol.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: MERIT: Mechanism-Driven Model Predicts Drug Outcomes and Nominates Indications for Failed Drugs
abstract: Drug development depends on efficacy and safety, but many trial-outcome prediction models incorporate trial design, prior development history, or compound identity, enabling compound memorization and inflating apparent performance. We developed MEchanism-Resolved Inference of Trial outcomes (MERIT), a model that predicts trial outcomes from molecular and disease features without using information on similar-compound success.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: A Witness for Quantum Correlations Using Nonlinear Spectroscopy
abstract: The ability to detect and quantify entanglement in molecular systems is essential for understanding their quantum correlations and to evaluating molecules as platforms for quantum technologies. Here we show how signals from existing spectroscopic techniques can provide sufficient information to witness entanglement. The main ingredient is a spectroscopic map from admissible quantum states to a finite-dimensional space of signal coefficients, which are expectation values of state-independent effective observables. The molecular response model and measurement protocol determine the effective observables for a fixed system bipartition, and the spectroscopic map defines sets of joint expectation values compatible with all admissible quantum states and their separable subset. We illustrate the construction of the effective observables and their expectation value sets using rotational invariants and the spectral structure of optical signals. Fluorescence dynamics and photon coincidences provide a complementary example. Our findings provide a theoretical basis for entanglement certification with established spectroscopic techniques.

title: Toward universal excited-state machine-learned potentials: a local excitation Hamiltonian for size consistency and transferability
abstract: Universal machine-learned interatomic potentials could make excited-state simulations across chemical space routine, but excitation energies, unlike ground-state energies, are not sums of atomic contributions. The excited states of noninteracting molecules are the union of their states, which pooled multistate readouts reproduce at best for the lowest state. We introduce LEH-MACE, whose excitation energies are the eigenvalues of a local excitation Hamiltonian assembled from atom-centred blocks, so this union holds exactly. We generated TD-DFT energies and forces for about 300,000 equilibrium, thermal, and excited-state geometries of over 100,000 molecules. LEH-MACE's advantage over direct readouts grew with the distance from the training data and was largest above $S_1$, with about half their $S_2$ and $S_3$ errors for long conjugated oligomers. For molecule pairs, only LEH-MACE kept its single-molecule accuracy, while a softmin readout remained superior for $S_1$ dynamics of larger chromophores. Exact size consistency is thus one step toward such potentials.

title: ProtLink: Sequence and Multispecies Graph Context for Protein Interaction Prediction
abstract: Predicting protein-protein interactions (PPIs) from sequence alone is difficult, while known interaction networks may provide informative biological context. We introduce ProtLink, a sequence-conditioned graph-learning framework that combines frozen ESM-2 representations with protein interaction topology and orthogroup-mediated connections between species. We compare sequence-only models, GraphSAGE, a homogeneous graph transformer, and a heterogeneous graph transformer (HGT) for human PPI prediction. In an initial edge-level comparison, three-layer multispecies HGT with ESM-2 650M features achieves an average precision (AP) of 0.980 under random negative sampling, compared with 0.951 for the homogeneous transformer; its AP decreases to 0.878 with two-hop-preferred negatives. In controlled three-seed experiments, three-layer full-graph HGT obtains an AP of $0.9701\pm0.0022$, exceeding an orthogroup-only model ($0.9435\pm0.0094$). The corresponding two-layer comparison shows little additional benefit from non-human PPI edges, consistent with the greater message-passing depth needed to transmit their information. For human proteins excluded from training interactions, multispecies HGT achieves $0.8335\pm0.0094$ AP versus $0.6482\pm0.0052$ for a sequence-only pair model. These results identify the value, depth dependence, and limits of evolutionary graph context while distinguishing prediction of held-out edges from generalization to held-out proteins.

title: Efficient Plane-to-Point Energy Transfer from Supramolecular Excitonic Systems to Molecular Acceptors
abstract: Collective excitonic interactions in supramolecular assemblies offer opportunities for efficient light harvesting and directed energy transport. Here, we demonstrate efficient energy transfer from two-dimensional silica-encapsulated TDBC J-aggregate sheets to covalently attached ATTO 590 molecular acceptors. Silica encapsulation preserves the J-aggregate excitonic properties while enabling acceptor functionalization at a defined separation from the donor plane. Steady-state donor quenching and acceptor sensitization yield energy-transfer efficiencies of 75-81% in solution, while time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal donor lifetime shortening. We develop a generalized Forster resonance energy-transfer model for an extended planar donor coupled to localized molecular acceptors, predicting an inverse fourth-power dependence of the transfer rate on donor-acceptor separation. Using experimental spectroscopic data and estimated structural parameters, the model predicts an energy-transfer rate of 4.77 x 10^10 s^-1, approximately ten times faster than the intrinsic donor decay rate, corresponding to a theoretical energy-transfer efficiency of approximately 91%. These findings provide a framework for developing hybrid excitonic architectures for light harvesting.

title: Quantifying Hidden Metabolites in 31P NMR Spectra by Physics-Based Spectral Subtraction
abstract: NMR spectroscopy enables reliable quantification of the metabolites present in a biological sample. The number of metabolites that can be assessed from NMR spectra is often limited by the intrinsically high complexity of the spectra, arising from the large number of molecules paired with their complex spectral patterns. 31P NMR based metabolomics embraces a reduced yet broad view of the metabolism and significantly facilitates the interpretation of the spectra due to a lower number of signals and a larger chemical shift dispersion. However, full quantification of metabolites can still be hindered by the presence of crowded regions. Here we exploit the fact that NMR lineshapes can be simulated precisely from quantum mechanical calculations for disentangling these crowded regions. Iterative subtraction of accurately simulated and fitted spectra of metabolites presenting isolated signals from the experimental spectrum yields meaningful residuals, enabling assignment and quantification of completely hidden metabolites. This approach ended at a noise-level residual spectrum, granting the full quantification of the 31P NMR spectrum. We implemented this approach in MR-SHIFT, a program developed in this work for spin Hamiltonian simulations and spectral fitting, which was then applied to the fully automated analysis of 31P NMR spectra of mouse tissues.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Direct Synthesis and Electrochemical Deintercalation of Mg-Intercalated Graphullerite
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) carbon allotropes have unique properties, synthetic tunability, and potential applications across several fields including catalysis, energy storage, and electronics. One such allotrope is the recently discovered graphullerite, which results from the oxidation and deintercalation of the layered rhombohedral fullerene polymer (Mg4C60)∞. The current synthetic approach to (Mg4C60)∞ is limited by low yield, phase impurity, and small crystal size, all of which preclude a comprehensive investigation of the physical and electronic properties of bulk graphullerite and its 2D…
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Intelligent computing neural network-driven analysis of maxwell trihybrid nanomaterial with chemical reactor optimization using STG model
abstract: This paper inspects the outcome of viscous dissipation on chemical reactive flow of Maxwell trihybrid nanoliquid with Darcy Forchheimer porous medium and Marangoni convection. The current model has considerable applications in progressive chemical and thermal engineering systems that demand improved heat and mass transfer. It has numerous applications, including electronic cooling devices, heat exchangers, chemical reactors, hydrometallurgical leaching systems, mineral slurry transport, and metallurgical activities. The addition of viscous dissipation and Joule heating makes the model applicable to electrically conducting fluids and high-temperature industrial processes such as electrowinning and smelting, while the Maxwell trihybrid nanoliquid increases thermal efficiency. Furthermore, the artificial neural network (ANN) structure allows for rapid prediction and enhancement of flow and heat transfer properties, making the model valuable for the design and control of modern energy and manufacturing systems. To train, test, and validate the model for precise flow behavior and thermal characteristic prediction, a reference dataset is created.The results demonstrate that the LMB-ANN technique provides fast convergence, high accuracy, and robust performance, making it a reliable and effective tool for optimizing complex industrial convection systems, including hydrometallurgical reactors and mineral slurry transport operations. The concentration profile for both trihybrid and hybrid nanofluids decreases as the chemical reaction parameter values increase.Clinical trial Number: Not applicable.

title: Descriptor Logic for Disorder in High-Entropy and Compositionally Complex Fluorite Oxides: A Critical Assessment
abstract: No single scalar captures disorder in high-entropy and compositionally complex fluorites. This Perspective evaluates compositional and structural descriptors by physical meaning, reference frame, covariance, and transferability. Pairwise cation mismatch contains the same information as size variance, whereas host-referenced misfit adds a reference-dependent mean-radius offset. Analysis of twenty-four published compositions from three systematic datasets illustrates the limits of configurational entropy and size variance as independent descriptors of phase formation and transport. With equal Hf, Zr, and Ce fractions, changing the host reference reverses misfit rankings and alters the host-offset term up to 78-fold. In twelve dual-phase zirconates and mixed zirconate-hafnates, the nominal rA/rB ratio correlates with phase fraction but describes neither coexisting phase, whereas measured phase compositions give non-overlapping fluorite and pyrochlore values, distinguishing descriptor limitations from inappropriate evaluation frames. Structural observables are assessed by specificity, reproducibility, and relevance. Together, these criteria and the compositional analysis define a framework that distinguishes compositional inputs, multiplicity and crystal-chemical mismatch, from their structural realization. Its purpose is to test descriptor relevance and limits rather than predict untested compositions.

title: Scalable MoS2/Si Photodiode Arrays from Roll-to-Roll Mechanical Exfoliation
abstract: We present a scalable, all-dry route to MoS2/Si photodiodes based on high-throughput roll-to-roll mechanical exfoliation. The method yields dense films of large-lateral-size MoS2 nanosheets and enables the formation of heterojunctions that operate in the photovoltaic regime when transferred onto locally etched Si regions. Individual devices show robust, fast photoresponses and broadband wavelength sensitivity. We further implemented a linear pixel array demonstrating position sensing capability and a 4x4 array as a proof-of-concept imaging sensor. These results indicate that roll-to-roll mechanical exfoliation can overcome common limitations of solution-processed films to enable low-cost, self-powered optoelectronic detectors for sensing and imaging applications.

title: HGSAF: Heterogeneous graph structural alignment and distillation model with attentive fusion for microbe-drug association prediction.
abstract: The rapid emergence of antimicrobial resistance necessitates AI-driven computational strategies to navigate the molecular diversity landscape of microbe-drug interactions. While graph neural networks have shown promise in predicting such associations, existing methods struggle with the intertwined challenges of processing topological and semantic features in isolation and handling severe class imbalance inherent in biomedical datasets. In this work, we devised a heterogeneous graph structural alignment and distillation with an attentive fusion model to predict microbe-drug associations.

title: Prediction of human intestinal passive membrane permeability using physiologically informed machine learning models.
abstract: Predicting human intestinal passive membrane permeability (Peff) is essential for reliable application of physiologically based biopharmaceutics models (PBBMs). Although in vitro cell-based assays and animal studies are widely used, their predictive performance is often limited by inter-laboratory variability and species differences. Furthermore, accurate prediction of intrinsic permeability requires consideration of physiological factors, particularly correction for the unstirred water layer (UWL) and exclusion of transporter-mediated transport.
venue: European journal of pharmaceutics and biopharmaceutics : official journal of Arbeitsgemeinschaft fur Pharmazeutische Verfahrenstechnik e.V

title: Geometry-Induced Construction of Sub-Stoichiometric 3D Covalent Organic Frameworks for SO2 Capture
abstract: Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) have emerged as a rapidly growing class of crystalline porous materials, yet reported structures adhere to the reticular chemistry paradigm of fully connected building blocks. Here, we report a geometry-induced construction strategy that enables the synthesis of sub-stoichiometric 3D COFs─JUC-748, JUC-749, and JUC-750─by deliberately combining building blocks with similar geometries but distinct connectivity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Frequency-Dependent Structural Responses of Amyloid-β Fibrils to Terahertz Pulses: A Nonequilibrium Molecular Dynamics Study
abstract: The abnormal aggregation of amyloid proteins into fibrils is closely associated with several neurodegenerative diseases, highlighting the importance of developing effective strategies to modulate fibril structural stability. Here, we employed nonequilibrium molecular dynamics(NEMD) simulations to examine the effects of intense terahertz-to-mid-infrared pulses on three amyloid fibrils (2LMP, 2MXU, and 5OQV), focusing on the combined effects of pulse frequency and electric-field strength. Frequency scans from 0.5 to 60 THz in 0.5 THz steps revealed frequency-dependent losses of {beta}-sheet content, with several common response patterns in these fibrils. Comparisons at 2, 23, 33, and 50 THz showed that pulse-induced changes in secondary structure differed from those in high-temperature controls. Hydrogen-bond analysis showed that total hydrogen-bond counts could partially recover even as interchain hydrogen bonds continued to decrease, with distinct responses among representative chain pairs. We therefore propose a two-threshold electric-field framework for fibril disruption: Eth1 describes the onset of structural perturbation, whereas Eth2 indicates persistent structural loss after the pulse. This framework offers a testable approach for characterizing amyloid structural responses to external fields, although the underlying energy-coupling mechanisms, quantitative thresholds, and long-term recovery require further validation. These findings may provide a theoretical basis for exploring external-field-based strategies to modulate protein aggregation.

title: Unseen but Avoidable: How Impurities Bias Electrocatalysis from Interface to Interpretation
abstract: Impurities exert profound effects on electrocatalytic measurements and interpretations. Trace levels of contaminants introduced through electrolytes, electrodes, gases, or cell materials routinely generate false activity signals, accelerate degradation, and alter product selectivity. This review categorizes impurity effects by functional impact, including misleading activity, compromised stability, and shifted selectivity, and offers strategies to recognize, isolate, and mitigate these influences.

title: Can AI Agents Reliably Optimize Computational Chemistry Codes?
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) approaches have opened new possibilities in computational and theoretical chemistry. AI agents can now execute computational workflows autonomously, and their use in scientific software development represents another promising direction. Herein, we present a general strategy for the controlled optimization of scientific software using a dual-agent harness. By using separate worker and controller agents for optimization and evaluation, respectively, we find that this approach can reduce computational costs while preserving numerical accuracy for the computational chemistry methods examined. We apply this strategy to TIP4P water simulations in LAMMPS, as well as to Coulomb and exchange matrix construction and linear-response time-dependent density functional theory (TDDFT) calculations in PySCF. Among these applications, the largest speedups are obtained for TDDFT. We then extend this strategy from optimizing established packages to developing efficient parallel CPU- and GPU-accelerated implementations of an initially serial molecular dynamics code, resulting in speedups of two to three orders of magnitude. Finally, we apply the protocol to open-ended algorithm development by constructing an adaptive self-consistent field approach that coordinates the use of multiple solvers. We find that the resulting approach can converge some challenging systems and occasionally reach lower-energy solutions than those obtained with the standalone solvers tested. These applications demonstrate that a strategy developed for improving code efficiency may also support the systematic development of computational methods. Overall, our benchmark study provides an example of AI-assisted advances in computational chemistry.

title: Fabrication and Characterization of Flexible In2O3 Thin-Film Transistors on Mica Substrates
abstract: Flexible oxide-semiconductor thin-film transistors (TFTs) with high field-effect mobility (uFE > 70 cm^2/Vs) are required for next-generation flexible displays. Polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs are promising candidates; however, conventional flexible substrates such as plastics are not suitable because their fabrication typically requires relatively high temperatures (~350 deg.C). In this study, we used mica as a flexible substrate to fabricate polycrystalline In2O3-based TFTs, motivated by previous demonstrations of crystalline oxide growth on mica. The resulting TFTs exhibited a uFE of approximately 75 cm^2/Vs. The devices maintained gate-modulated operation after 10^3 flex-out bending cycles at a 5 mm radius, whereas flex-in cycling caused early electrical failure, likely due to In2O3 film degradation. The TFTs also operated normally after exposure to 85 deg.C and 40% relative humidity for one day. These results demonstrate that mica substrates enable high-mobility, flex-out-compatible In2O3-based TFTs.

title: Quantitative Assessment of Crystal Structure Prediction
abstract: Crystal Structure Prediction (CSP) aims to predict a material's 3D structure from its chemical composition, with applications from energy storage to biomedical devices. Despite its importance, existing evaluation frameworks suffer from key limitations: they rely on threshold-sensitive or incomparable metrics, focus predominantly on geometric performance while overlooking physical plausibility, and fail to account for polymorphism, where a chemical composition can crystallize into multiple stable structures. In parallel, recent Symmetry-Informed CSP (SICSP) methods often report results alongside standard CSP baselines while receiving crystallographic templates at inference, which constrain the search space and make SICSP a fundamentally different task. To address these limitations, we introduce an Orientation-invariant, Polymorph-Aware, Large Benchmark (OPAL-Bench) that evaluates CSP and SICSP as separate tasks. We evaluate 7 CSP and 2 SICSP methods under OPAL-Bench across 4 datasets using threshold-free geometric and physical distance metrics. Our results show that no method dominates across all metrics, and that geometric performance is not strongly correlated with physical plausibility. We also release OPAL-CSP, an SE(3)-equivariant flow-matching baseline for the CSP track that performs competitively on geometric metrics and ranks among the best on physical ones. By unifying geometric and physical metrics under a polymorph-aware protocol, OPAL-Bench enables a more comprehensive assessment of generative quality in CSP.

title: Unleashing the potential of saturation-transfer MR fingerprinting (ST-MRF) in neuro-oncology: quantitative molecular CEST and MTC mapping.
abstract: Neuro-oncology biomarkers allow probing tissues beyond anatomical or relaxation contrast. However, new techniques are needed to achieve mechanistic elucidation and effective therapeutic interventions. Quantitative MRI techniques, such as T1, T2, diffusion, and perfusion imaging, provide insights into tumor biology, infiltration, microstructure, and hemodynamics, and have been implemented clinically, but are limited in probing cellular and molecular changes.

title: Large Language Models in Chemistry: Opportunities, Limitations, and Hallucination Risks
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have moved quickly from general-purpose text tools to components of chemical research workflows. They are now used to extract data from the literature, propose synthesis routes, write analysis code, predict properties from few examples, and control laboratory instruments through tool-augmented agents. These capabilities create real opportunities, particularly for researchers and institutions with limited access to specialist software and training. They also carry risks that are specific to chemistry.

title: De Novo Design of Catalytically Active Salen-Binding Proteins
abstract: De novo design of catalytic metalloproteins has the potential to generate enzymes that combine the efficiency of natural proteins with the reactivity of synthetic organometallic catalysts. Here, we develop a computational strategy to design enzymes with novel tertiary structures that bind metal salen complexes, classic small-molecule catalysts not found in biology. Six proteins were designed and screened for function; five of six express well, bind a Co-salen cofactor, and catalyze a transition metal hydrogen atom transfer (MHAT)-mediated deallylation reaction, representing the first de novo proteins to catalyze this class of transformation. The spectroscopic properties and crystal structure of the most active sequence were in excellent agreement with the design, and the holoprotein retained its structure and activity over a broad range of pH (2–12), temperatures up to 95 °C, and aqueous/organic solvent mixtures. We suggest that the combinatorial space provided by metal ion identity, ligand substitution, and active site structure can be used to generate artificial metalloenzymes that catalyze many chemical transformations.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Clinical Evidence-Guided Residual Learning for Medication Recommendation with Dynamic DDI Regularization
abstract: Medication recommendation must combine patient-specific treatment evidence with the interaction structure of a prescription. The central challenge is to determine which evidence supports each medication and how strongly to regularize interactions while preserving predictive quality. We propose EviDrug, a clinical evidence-guided residual learning framework. Its clinical-memory backbone integrates a self-trained visit-aware encoder, training-case memory and one medication-set interaction block to establish a patient-specific prescription. A gated refinement head combines the backbone states with clinical associations and history-conditioned medication identities through bounded logit corrections. Drug-drug interaction (DDI) feedback adapts regularization strength using training-query predictions. Across MIMIC-IV, NWICU and SICdb, EviDrug leads twelve published-method baselines in AP, F1 and Jaccard, improving AP by 2.26, 2.06 and 1.71 percentage points over the strongest comparator. These gains come at lower parameter and runtime costs than MetaDrug. Matched controls demonstrate DDI reductions with stable predictive quality. Code is available at https://github.com/LIZESHENG13/EviDrug.

title: Efficient LLM Adaptation with Forward-Only Passes
abstract: Large language model (LLM) inference serving is undergoing rapid growth and large-scale deployment, motivating us to rethink how the inference process itself can be leveraged to enable efficient task-specific LLM adaptation. In this paper, we propose a forward-only approach for efficient LLM adaptation with forward-only passes in LLM inference serving. We exploit the angle concentration of activations induced by each singular value decomposition (SVD) component to measure its contribution-dispersed or concentrated-to the angle concentration of the hidden states. Based on this, our forward-only search then efficiently identifies the weight matrix with the highest dispersion that merits rank reduction. We then selectively remove the higher-order components and retain the lower-order components in SVD. Empirical results across diverse datasets demonstrate the competitive accuracy of our forward-only approach, while theoretical analysis shows lower peak memory and greater speedup than the gradient-based approach and greater speedup than the exhaustive search approach. The experiments further present the robustness and generalization of our forward-only approach to various LLMs with up to 57B parameters. The code is included in the supplementary material.

title: DFT-Agent Bench: Scaffold Effects and Execution Provenance in Autonomous DFT
abstract: Large language models are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents for first-principles materials simulation. We report empirical findings from DFT-Agent Bench, a benchmark of 200+ Quantum ESPRESSO tasks spanning relaxation, electronic structure, equation-of-state, and elastic-tensor pipelines over multiple material tiers. Each task carries a QE-derived ground truth with public-reference cross-checks where available, and a provenance audit checks whether the required QE execution contract was met. Under one execution harness, we compare a near-bare ReAct baseline with a bundled v5.1 scaffold on two models. The complete scaffold improves bands+DOS by +0.08/+0.11 and d-electron vc-relax by +0.17 on both models, while high-scoring relaxation and equation-of-state cells leave little room for improvement. The elastic result is model-dependent (0.18 to 0.40 for deepseek-v4-pro and 0.62 to 0.59 for claude-opus-4-8). A fixed 100-task analysis with retrieval disabled supports the aggregate pattern: the fully frozen DeepSeek comparison gains +0.17, while the Opus comparison gains +0.10 against a historical pool baseline (p < 0.001). The provenance gate catches incomplete or unmarked executions that can receive high rubric scores; it is an execution-contract check, not a test for intentional fraud. These results characterize the evaluated DFT workflows. The anonymous review artifact contains the frozen diagnostic slice, prompts, scorer, and solver revisions: https://anonymous.4open.science/r/231e31re91287h/README.md.

title: Computational Compound Prioritization Strategy Incorporating Docking Variability and Interaction Energies Identifies Putative LRH-1 Binders
abstract: Compound ranking in structure-based computer-aided drug discovery notoriously yields highly ranked false positives due to sampling and, more frequently, scoring errors. We developed a compound prioritization strategy that utilizes sampled docked poses from complementary docking approaches, i.e., targeted physics-based docking and blind docking with a generative model, into multiple conformations of the target protein to train two multilayer perceptron (MLP) models. The MLPs predict binders or activators at the orthosteric ligand-binding pocket of the nuclear receptor Liver Receptor Homologue-1 (LRH-1, NR5A2). Our approach circumvents the reliance on a single docked pose for scoring compounds or individual scoring metrics for compound ranking. In an out-of-distribution compound set, we observed that the MLPs identified compounds that are chemically dissimilar from those in the training set and are sensitive to single scaffold modifications, making the MLPs potential tools for lead optimization. We applied the MLPs on a pilot study prospective drug discovery campaign, which resulted in the identification of four putative LRH-1 binders. We found that a combination of scoring and prediction metrics enriches for hit compounds across library sizes. In all, this work presents a method to leverage structural and experimental data to aid drug discovery for a challenging protein target.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Universal Approximation by Equivariant Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks with a Bilinear Readout
abstract: We prove universal approximation for the bilinear-readout equivariant message-passing network (BREMP), a reference architecture for equivariant graph neural network interatomic potentials. Its layers combine equivariant convolutions with affine maps, and its readout forms invariants from products of the equivariant features. We construct a one-layer feature that determines the local environment up to permutations of atoms of the same type. The construction uses spherical harmonic filters of degree no larger than the largest number of neighbors at a common distance from the center. Iterating the construction recovers the environment reachable in as many hops as there are layers, using the same bound on filter degrees at the layer cutoff. The readout approximates every continuous invariant function of the features uniformly on compact sets. Together these give universal approximation of atomic energies at a prescribed physical range using a shorter layer cutoff. We assume that, throughout the admissible class, message passing reaches all neighbors in each physical environment within a common number of layers. Finally, DPA4, an interatomic potential architecture in production use, inherits this result by approximating the BREMP layers constructed in the proof and realizing the bilinear readout.

title: BlenderFORGE: Framework for Optimizing Reactive 3D-Graphics Editing Ability of MLLMs
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown promise as interactive agents, yet precise, programmatic 3D graphics editing remains difficult to train because existing systems largely rely on closed-source model APIs and lack deterministic, state-verifiable execution environments. We present BlenderFORGE, a trainable data-environment-optimization framework for open-weight MLLM agents that edit explicit Blender scenes through Blender Python (bpy) code generation. BlenderFORGE targets four fundamental state-verifiable editing task families: object placement, shape-key editing, lighting adjustment, and material modification. It integrates three components: (1) a scalable perturbation-based data generation pipeline built from curated assets and large-scale 3D scene repositories; (2) an isolated Blender Sandbox for deterministic code execution, structured state export, and closed-loop reward computation; and (3) a two-stage training pipeline that uses offline teacher trajectories for cold-start Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and sandbox-computed rewards for multi-turn tool-agentic Reinforcement Learning (AgentLoop-RL). Experiments across the four task families show that the resulting open-weight Qwen3-VL-8B and Qwen3.5-9B BlenderFORGE agents substantially improve over their base models and achieve competitive performance with several zero-shot proprietary MLLM baselines on selected metrics. Additional cross-benchmark evaluations and camera-reframing experiments provide evidence of transfer beyond the original training setting.

title: Symmetry-Induced Conservation Laws, Three-Channel Attribution, and Solid-Phase Recycling in Prebiotic Enantiomeric Excess Amplification
abstract: Enantiomeric excess ($\mathrm{ee}$) is the primary observable used to quantify chiral amplification across prebiotic chemistry, asymmetric autocatalysis, and multiphase crystallization. Because $\mathrm{ee} = Δ/ M$ is the ratio of net chiral excess $Δ= L - D$ to total chiral mass $M = L + D$, identical increases in $\mathrm{ee}$ can arise either by generating net chiral excess through parity-breaking reactions or by depleting total chiral mass through symmetric phase or oligomer partitioning. Here we establish a pathwise conservation law and a model-free three-channel attribution identity for $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric reaction networks. In any closed network without autocatalytic feedback or epimerization, net chiral excess is conserved along every stochastic trajectory ($Δ(t) = Δ(0)$), locking liquid-phase amplification to cumulative mass loss ($\mathrm{ee}_f = \mathrm{ee}_0 M_0 / M_f$). Re-analyzing seven experimental systems shows that standalone phase removal (Channel R) loses $91.7\%$--$98.9\%$ of chiral solute into racemic sediment in closed batches and washes out under open racemic inflow. Coupling eutectic partitioning (Channel R) with solid/solution racemization recycling (Channel B) converts the precipitated solid into homochiral product ($96.5\%$ recoverable homochiral crystal mass at $96.5\%$ total and $100.0\%$ solid $\mathrm{ee}$), whereas coupling evaporative concentration with liquid-phase autocatalysis crosses the open-flow bifurcation threshold against continuous racemic dilution ($81.9\%$ homochiral yield at $92.9\%$ active chiral $\mathrm{ee}$). We further establish non-crossing parity invariants for dual-monomer networks, derive a closed-form wet--dry amplification law, and resolve a one-dimensional identifiability ridge in chiral mineral adsorption via antipodal crystal-pair protocols.

title: The Future of Light-Emitting Materials
Dynamic Molecular Transformation Mediated Crystallization Regulation and Interface Passivation in Tin Based Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: Tin-based perovskites are promising candidates for lead-free photovoltaics but suffer from labile Sn$^{2+}$ coordination, rapid crystallization, and severe interfacial defects. Here, we develop a dynamic molecular transformation using 1-acetylpiperazine (PX) to regulate crystallization and interface chemistry simultaneously. During nucleation and growth, the carbonyl group coordinates with Sn$^{2+}$ to stabilize precursor complexes, moderate supersaturation, and enable controlled crystal growth. Upon annealing, PX undergoes in situ molecular transformation, suggested to form amidinium-functionalized species that preferentially occupy surface A-site vacancies, forming a passivation layer and suppressing nonradiative recombination. This coupled bulk-to-interface evolution yields compact, highly crystalline films with improved optoelectronic quality. Devices achieve a power conversion efficiency of 15.18% and retain 94.1% of initial efficiency after 500 h of continuous illumination. This work demonstrates a dynamic molecular engineering approach integrating crystallization control and interface passivation, providing a pathway toward efficient and stable lead-free perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Efficient and Accurate Zero Shot Generation of Symmetric Protein Complexes
abstract: Symmetric organization is a fundamental principle of biomolecular complex assembly. The same principle underlies engineered applications, from vaccine platforms to nanomaterials, making symmetric de novo generation a core capability for computational protein design. We establish a theoretical foundation equating generation of an assembly with underlying symmetry group $G$ to generation within a quotient space over $G$. This directly allows $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant models to generate symmetric structures with minimal distribution shift. With this insight we introduce ZeUS ($\textbf{Ze}$ro-shot $\textbf{U}$nified $\textbf{S}$ymmetrization), a framework that converts any pretrained $\mathrm{SE}(3)$-equivariant backbone generative model into an efficient generator of symmetric assemblies with no retraining. ZeUS operates on a single $\textit{canonical subunit}$ and utilizes $\textit{phantom subunits}$ to preserve internal model operations, reducing memory and runtime cost by $\mathcal{O}(|G|)$ for finite groups $G$, compared to a full-complex forward pass. We implement ZeUS for IPA-based models (FrameDiff, FoldFlow) and axial-attention-based RFdiffusion, showing high generation efficiency with minimal degradation to generation quality. We then apply ZeUS to generate symmetric complexes of over $10{,}000$ residues with exact, untruncated attention, a scale previously intractable with any model.

title: Multifractality in sputtered crystalline and amorphous transition metal nitride thin films
abstract: In this work, we present evidence for multifractal growth in Titanium and Niobium nitride thin films on different substrates. Self-similar multifractal structures such as dendrites and multi-branched snowflake-like structures are reported. The fractal dimensions are controlled by a combination of processing parameters and conditions at the film-substrate interface. Significantly, fractal growth is observed not only in crystalline films on crystalline and amorphous substrates but also on amorphous films on crystalline substrates. The 2D Multifractal Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (2D MFDFA) carried out on the scanning electron micrographs, clearly reveals the multifractal nature of the nitride thin films. The statistical moments were varied between -5 to +5. The Hausdorff dimensions for the TiN films are in the range of 1.65 to 1.79 while it is 1.64 to 1.74 for the NbN thin films. It is proposed that the observed multifractality is due to a competition between morphological instabilities and Diffusion-Limited Aggregation

title: Track or Follow? A Jev-Compatible Multi-Agent Trading System When Web News Lags the Market
abstract: LLM agents increasingly trade on the Web news they read, yet much Web news about listed firms is published after, and about, the price move it reports, so a reader can agree with the market by following it instead of reading the event. We ask whether LLM judgments of Web news track the market's reaction to the reported event or follow it. To answer, we built a multi-agent trading system whose agents share only point-in-time stores and answer typed questions through the interface of Jev, a hosted typed decision model; code sets every position under a proved bound on how far text can move it. In a hash-committed test of a Jev-compatible reader built from a pinned LLM's option probabilities, item judgments track announcement-window abnormal returns (weekly Spearman 0.119), also after the LLM's release, and event types agree with the issuers' 8-K filings (AUC 0.833); Jev's judgments of news published after its own release track the reaction as well (descriptive). Exploratory analyses show where the association comes from: 72% of earnings news items appear after the issuer's filing, contributor-written items often report the price move, and from the first trade after publication the association falls to 0.023. At a weekly horizon, the confirmatory test detects no rank information over code-only features. Under attack, decision cards traced 88% of successful attacks to the planted item. We propose that market-graded tests of Web-text readers report the criterion from publication, not only from the event.

title: Dopant Cluster Engineering for Tunable Room-Temperature Ferromagnetism in 2D Transition Metal Dichalcogenides
abstract: Two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides (2D-TMDs) offer a promising platform for realizing dilute magnetic semiconductors. However, simultaneously achieving large magnetic anisotropy energy (MAE) and high Curie temperature (T$_\text{c}$) remains a major challenge. In this work, we employ DFT+U to systematically investigate the thermodynamic stability and magnetic properties of 2D-MoSe$_2$ and 2D-WSe$_2$ doped with transition metal atoms. We found that the paired dopant configurations are more stable than previously attributed isolated dopants. Despite their nearly identical crystal structures, 2D-MoSe$_2$ and 2D-WSe$_2$ show contrasting properties upon doping. All paired dopants in 2D-MoSe$_2$ exhibit long-range ferromagnetic coupling (FMC) primarily due to carrier-mediated exchange interactions, whereas those in 2D-WSe$_2$ show weak exchange coupling. Interestingly, 2Mn$_\text{2W}$ shows a transition from less stable antiferromagnetic coupling (AFMC) in the short range to highly stable FMC in the long-range. The combined effect of spin-orbit coupling, exchange interactions, and orbital hybridization gives rise to a large MAE with maximum in-plane values of $-$3.5 meV for 2V$_\text{2Mo}$ and $-$3.2 meV for 2Mn$_\text{2W}$. Monte Carlo simulations estimate T$_\text{c}$ $\simeq$ 440 K for 2Fe$_\text{2Mo}$ and ensure its high-temperature stability in 2D-MoSe$_2$. Our results establish dopant clustering as an effective route to engineer high-temperature ferromagnetism in 2D-TMDs and highlight their potential for nano-spintronic applications.

title: EmbodiedIntentBench: Benchmarking Intent-Driven Runtime Adaptation for Mobile Robotic Missions
abstract: Mobile robotic sensing systems must adapt to operator requirements, limited resources, changing connectivity, and observation opportunities shaped by physical motion. Evaluating runtime strategies therefore requires assessing whether their decisions fulfill mission objectives, beyond isolated perception accuracy or execution efficiency. We present EmbodiedIntentBench, a benchmark for intent-driven runtime adaptation in mobile robotic missions. It represents mission intent through structured contracts for coverage, temporal evidence, reporting, urgency, and resources, and couples simulated unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) workloads with causal, resource-accounted execution. Computation decisions affect mission time, resource use, and which observations can contribute evidence. We evaluate fixed and adaptive perception strategies in multi-phase missions and under changing urgency, connectivity, and battery conditions. In the multi-phase Depot study, a configuration with 87.5% full-bank target recall across visible target observations completes only 1 of 16 missions, whereas a lower-recall configuration completes 14. In an ablation, ignoring execution-induced observation loss increases aggregate mission success and reverses the ordering of two runtime strategies. Replays using Jetson AGX Orin CPU and GPU profiles change the relative success of local and remote strategies. In selected Jetson GPU-profile replays, intent-driven adaptation reduces modeled task energy by up to 28% with unchanged mission success. EmbodiedIntentBench provides an extensible framework for evaluating runtime decisions against mission fulfillment under physical and resource constraints.

title: Ultrastretchable, Tissue-Matched Piezoelectric Gel with Preferentially Oriented Molecular Ferroelectric Crystallization
abstract: Molecular ferroelectrics hold great potential for bioelectronics because of their excellent piezoelectric responses and biocompatibility. However, conventional integration into gel matrices suffers from two major drawbacks: solvent evaporation methods often yield brittle films with poor modulus matching with soft tissues, whereas physical blending typically leads to filler agglomeration and random crystal dispersion, making it difficult to achieve preferential crystal orientation and thereby limiting the piezoelectric performance.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Pixels over Symbols: Sensory Realism Improves Behavioral Alignment in Models of Cognition
abstract: Computational models of cognition have traditionally relied on abstract symbolic inputs that approximate sensory experiences with simplified vector representations. This simplification reflects historical computational constraints and a long-held assumption that the details of sensory realism are incidental to the study of cognitive processes. Recent advances have enabled the development of sensory-realistic models capable of performing diverse cognitive tasks, yet whether sensory realism meaningfully shapes cognition has not been formally established. We address this gap through a large-scale empirical comparison of abstract and sensory-realistic neural network models trained on a battery of memory-dependent decision-making tasks. Our results show that sensory-realistic models mirror human behavioral response patterns significantly more than their abstract counterparts, though a substantial gap to human internal behavioral consistency remains even for the best tested models. By analyzing the internal dynamics of these systems, we find that the learned recurrent weights are not the main source of this divergence. In fact, frozen abstract-trained weights driven by sensory-realistic inputs recover the human consistency of sensory-realistic models. The resulting dynamics are also within the seed-to-seed variability of sensory-realistic models. Together, our findings argue that across a broad set of visual working-memory tasks, sensory realism accounts for a substantial portion of the model-human behavioral agreement, more than the choice of sequence architecture and comparable to the choice of vision encoder. These results suggest that findings obtained from abstract task models in neuroscience should be more carefully interpreted in light of their potential behavioral limitations.

title: Symmetry and Redundancy in Cremer-Pople Phases for Ring Puckering
abstract: Cremer-Pople (CP) coordinates provide an exact description of ring puckering, yet direct sampling of their phases generates many symmetry-equivalent representations of the same puckering pattern. We develop a general analytical framework that identifies these equivalences before Cartesian reconstruction and geometry optimization. For homogeneous rings of arbitrary size, explicit transformations of the CP phases and the signed special coordinate of even-membered rings generate the complete symmetry orbit of the ordered elevation pattern. We classify the redundancies into four types and derive a factorized orbit-size formula linking CP multiplicity to puckering symmetry. These results yield exact single-phase fundamental intervals and sequentially reduced multiphase covering domains, including the restriction to a positive special coordinate. The framework is extended to rings containing one heteroatom or two identical heteroatoms, with reductions determined by the operations that preserve their placement. We also introduce a semidiscrete conformational nomenclature that combines symbolic amplitude distributions with explicit active phases. In an application to cyclohexadecane, symmetry reduction alone decreases the number of sampled CP points by approximately a factor of thirty. Combined with selective phase-grid coarsening for three ordinary modes, the reduction approaches two orders of magnitude. These developments provide a systematic basis for generating, classifying, and efficiently sampling ring puckering patterns in CP space.

title: Spatiotemporal Energy Consistency Enables Reliable Coarse-Grained Molecular Dynamics from Diffusion Models
abstract: Coarse-grained molecular dynamics (CGMD) extends molecular simulations to length and time scales inaccessible to atomistic models, but building thermodynamically faithful CG potentials remains a longstanding challenge. Energy-based diffusion models (EBDMs) provide a promising route for learning CG potentials through their zero-time energy. However, CGMD driven by diffusion-learned potentials can produce equilibrium ensembles that deviate substantially from the target distribution. We show that the zero-time distribution error is bounded by the sum of the spatial score error and temporal energy-derivative error, whereas conventional diffusion objectives directly supervise only the spatial component. Based on this finding, we introduce Spatiotemporal Energy Consistency (STEC) supervision, which complements spatial score matching by explicitly constraining temporal energy derivatives. We derive an exact and tractable objective for this temporal component, avoiding the substantial computational overhead associated with previous regularization schemes. Across peptide and fast-folding protein systems, STEC-trained EBDMs accurately reproduce equilibrium distributions with free-energy errors within chemical accuracy, while supporting stable long-time simulations that recover key metastable transition patterns. On held-out octapeptides, STEC reduces free-energy errors by more than 5-fold relative to the strongest competing baseline, while achieving a median production-cost reduction of approximately 1,700-fold relative to atomistic molecular dynamics under a defined structural-coverage benchmark. These results establish STEC as a scalable framework for learning thermodynamically reliable CG force fields for increasingly complex biomolecular systems.

title: Imperfectly Imperfect: Evaluating Graded Cognitive Diversity in LLM Persona Simulations
abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used as synthetic participants in social, behavioural, and decision-making research, yet it remains unclear whether they can express graded cognitive diversity as assigned when engaging in simulated behaviour. We introduce a cognition-suite evaluation that tests whether simulated populations reproduce human variation in reasoning, self-reported traits, their associations, and downstream behaviour. Agents conditioned on synthetic or human-derived profiles of cognitive reflection, Need for Cognition, and Big Five personality answer the same suite as a cohort of 473 adults: two newly assembled tests, a Cognitive Reflection Test (CRT) and a Behavioural Reflection Test (BRT) whose decision scenarios measure reflection in behaviour, alongside an established CRT and the two trait questionnaires. Across seven full-battery simulation runs of four models, agents recover Need for Cognition and Big Five trait distributions on self-report questionnaires, but fall short on simulating diversity of cognitive task performance and downstream behaviours. In the four Claude Sonnet 4.6 runs, every agent scores full marks on both CRTs, whatever reflection level its persona was assigned. In the other three runs agents make intuitive-lure errors (the tempting wrong answers CRT items invite), but 49 to 85% score full marks, against under 10% in the human sample. Claude Sonnet 5 comes closest to people's item-by-item pattern of lures; the other two runs give fewer lures and vary less between items. In the BRT scenarios, every run over-produces 8 to 11 of 15 coded behaviours by at least 20 percentage points, and people's links between reflection and behaviour carry over only in part. Useful synthetic populations must preserve not only trait descriptors but the structured variation in reasoning, error type, and behaviour those descriptors are meant to organise.

title: Coupled plasmonic Fabry-Perot resonances modulating electromagnetic enhancement at a silver nanowire-nanoparticle junction proved by surface-enhanced fluorescence spectroscopy
abstract: We investigated the surface-enhanced fluorescence (SEF), which is the broad background spectrum underlying the surface-enhanced resonant Raman scattering of dye molecules, emitted from junctions between silver nanoparticles (NPs) and nanowires (NWs). We found that the electromagnetic enhancement factors (FR) derived from the SEF exhibited spectral modulation, such as complicated oscillatory structures. This property became clearer when the emission polarization was perpendicular to the long axis of the NWs. The FR spectra of the long and short NWs exhibit fine and broad oscillatory structures, respectively, when the NPs are positioned near the NW centers. When the NPs were near the NW ends, a combination of fine and broad structures was observed. Numerical calculations of the position-dependent FR spectra successfully reproduced these properties, indicating that the spectral properties originated from the interaction between two plasmonic Fabry-Perot (FP) resonators within the NW, separated by a NP. Based on this result, an analytical model of coupled FP resonators was developed to evaluate these spectral features using experimentally measured NW lengths and NP positions while varying the inter-resonator coupling efficiency. This analysis revealed that the interference and superposition of the two FP resonances resulted in these complex spectra, the energy of which was radiated by the localized plasmons of the NPs.

title: Delta-Corrected Shot Reduction for Bypassing Optimization Plateaus in Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
abstract: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) remains a cornerstone hybrid quantum-classical algorithm for quantum simulation, yet its scalability is fundamentally constrained by heavy measurement overheads. While strategies such as variance-preserved shot reduction (VPSR) mitigates this cost, they suffer from convergence instability and optimization stagnation caused by finite-sample bias in limited pilot shots. To overcome this limitation, we introduce delta-corrected shot reduction (DCSR), an analytically enhanced shot allocation strategy that rigorously mitigates finite-sample instability. Utilizing the multivariate delta method, we derive explicit higher-order bias correction terms for the empirical reduction factor. Both theoretical analysis and numerical simulations reveal that incorporating higher-order statistical moments, such as skewness and kurtosis, provides the gradient resolution necessary to bypass noise-induced barren plateaus. DSCR significantly accelerates convergence compared to standard VPSR across diverse noise and resource regimes while matching or decreasing cumulative measurement costs, establishing a mathematically rigorous framework for variance-stabilized shot allocation on near-term hardware.

title: A Computational Framework for the Determination of the Binding Affinity of Peripheral Proteins to Homogeneous Membranes
abstract: Peripheral membrane-binding proteins (PMPs) are essential to immunological and neurological processes, and disruptions in their membrane interactions are implicated in cancer, neurodegeneration, and autoimmune diseases. Their functional diversity arises from the wide range of mechanisms by which they associate with lipid surfaces, motivating atomistic computational frameworks capable of quantifying binding energetics.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Multi-omics indicating the risk of organochlorines to liver cancer.
abstract: The incidence and mortality rates of liver cancer remain consistently high worldwide, with China having the highest rates globally. The causes of liver cancer are multifactorial. This study focuses on identifying specific targets that continuously contribute to cellular damage after exposure to environmental organic chlorine compounds (OCCs), ultimately increasing the risk of liver cancer development. Liver cancer-related data were obtained from the GEO and TCGA databases. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were analyzed using the "limma" package in R.

title: A data-driven approach for systematic correction of electronic bandgaps
abstract: We demonstrate that a single machine-learning correction, applied to bandgaps from density functional theory calculations with two of the most frequently used energy functionals, results in bandgaps that are close to the experimental values. This solves a classical problem of computationally efficient electronic structure methods, to give reliable bandgaps that can be compared to experiments. The employed approach relies on materials specific feature engineering of machine learning models, and is shown to have close accuracy to that of much more expensive calculations based on the GW-approximation or hybrid functionals. The findings reported here open the possibility to use efficient calculations in materials design workflows that need reliable bandgaps, with implications for investigations targeting large computational databases or for investigations that are entirely predictive in nature.

title: A Geometry-Guided Feature-Space Framework for Interpretable Unsupervised 4D-STEM Analysis of Complex Multiphase Materials
abstract: Rapid, high-fidelity analysis of four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4D-STEM) datasets from heterogeneous materials remains challenging because coexisting phases, orientation variants, local strain gradients, and intrinsic TEM thin-foil effects produce complex, overlapping diffraction signatures. Here, we present a machine-learning (ML) framework that combines physics-informed geometric descriptors with weighted high-dimensional embeddings to identify latent structural patterns with minimal prior knowledge. By constructing a regularized descriptor space before embedding and density-based clustering, the method improves cluster stability, suppresses noise-driven fragmentation, and reduces sensitivity to embedding hyperparameters. Spatial weighting produced the largest stability gain, increasing median cluster persistence from 0.04 to 0.55 while reducing the noise fraction from approximately 22% to 0%. Rotation weighting increased DBCV from 0.80 to 0.92, although the noise fraction rose from 0.2% to 1.0%, highlighting a trade-off between improved density separation and noise rejection. We validate the framework on two benchmark systems: Si/Si$_x$Ge$_{1-x}$ epitaxial layers with continuous lattice variation and deformation, and multiphase Ti-Nb alloys containing distinct phases and orientation variants. Comparisons with a pretrained vanilla autoencoder and model-free pattern vectorization show that the physics-informed geometric descriptor provides higher cluster fidelity, greater interpretability, and substantially lower dimensionality.

title: Atomic-Scale Insights into Electron-Driven Ag Migration and Growth Across Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8/Ag2SeO3 Interfaces: A Theoretical and Experimental Study
abstract: The ZIF-8/Ag2SeO3 heterostructure was designed to combine the adsorption capacity and porous architecture of zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8) with the multifunctional response of Ag2SeO3 (ASO), seeking synergistic interactions that could yield a material with enhanced, complementary functionalities. We report the synthesis and interfacial evolution of ZIF-8/ASO heterostructures and the in situ formation of metallic Ag nanoparticles (NPs) under electron irradiation. X-ray diffraction confirms the coexistence of cubic ZIF-8 (I43m) and monoclinic ASO (P21/c) phases, with a microstructure consisting of ZIF-8 NPs uniformly anchored on ASO microrods in intimate interfacial contact. Time-resolved electron microscopy directly captures the nucleation and growth of Ag NPs on the ZIF-8 surface during electron irradiation, as confirmed by HRTEM-SAED and elemental maps, indicating spatially confined cubic Ag NPs with exposed (111) and (200) planes. Photoluminescence measurements show pronounced emission quenching and spectral redistribution, indicating modified optoelectronic behavior following heterostructure formation. First-principles calculations identify the ZIF-8/ASO(010) interface as a favorable configuration, characterized by strong interfacial interaction and significant charge redistribution. These results are consistent with the experimentally observed localized formation of Ag NPs and suggest that interfacial electronic interactions contribute to Ag+ reduction. Overall, the ZIF-8/ASO heterostructure provides an electron-responsive platform for localized Ag NP formation and interfacial optoelectronic modulation, offering insights into electron-beam-induced processes in ZIF-8-based heterostructures.

title: Template-Guided Crystal Chemical Design of Eu2+-Activated La2Ca3[Si4N4O8] Oxonitridosilicate Phosphor
abstract: Template-guided crystal-chemical design offers a route to oxonitridosilicates, but transfer of an oxide topology requires compatible cation coordination and charge balance. Here, we report the synthesis and structural characterization of the 6-ring host La2Ca3[Si4N4O8], designed by considering [SiN]+ for [AlO]+ substitution in the Ca3[Al2O6] template together with aliovalent La3+/Ca2+ substitution. The idealized structural description contains isolated rings of corner-sharing [SiN2O2] tetrahedra and partially occupied or vacant cation sites.

title: Lifting mechanical zero modes without dispersion
abstract: Floppy frameworks carry flat bands of zero-frequency mechanisms with no finite-frequency resonance, and couplings that lift them usually spread them. We show that an on-site tensor lifts a mechanism band without first-order dispersion exactly when, projected onto the mechanisms, it acts as wavevector-independent scalars on orthogonal pieces. Three structures achieve this: local normal modes, invariant symmetry sectors, and a balance law. A mechanism moves both ends of every bond between two vertex classes equally along it, and where the inter-class bond tensors are class scalars this balance law fixes its norm shares and hence the flat value from geometry alone. For the fluorite net the band lies outside the tensor spectrum, at 14/9 of the contact stiffness to first order, and stays flat to all orders in a fixed cage. A placement inside a tiling dual that keeps the common symmetry supplies such tensors, because each contact star inherits its site symmetry. Ten catalogued dual pairs lift flat; half are eigenvalue cases a resolved count matches, and the balance law explains flat bands in random cages too. Duality makes the rigid cage common. In a printable beam-frame lattice, contacts that lock joint rotation remove first-order bending dispersion whenever bonded mechanisms are orthogonal local normals.

title: In-Band Boundary Resonances from Coalescing Zero-Group-Velocity Points
abstract: Boundary states generally reside in band gaps, whereas in-band confinement typically requires exact decoupling from propagating modes. We demonstrate an alternative mechanism in reciprocal, topologically trivial Hermitian lattices arising from the coalescence of two zero-group-velocity (ZGV) points. At coalescence, the group velocity and inverse effective mass vanish simultaneously, and the corresponding Bloch root acquires higher multiplicity. The coalesced root remains propagating, whereas nearby root splitting yields weakly evanescent channels that, together with a bulk-matched termination, generate a boundary-weighted resonance within the propagating spectrum. The mechanism is realized analytically in a two-leg ladder model through the coalescence of time-reversal-related ZGVs and extends to distinct ZGVs produced by longer-range interactions. Finite-size scaling distinguishes the resulting resonance from extended and defect-bound states. Scanning laser Doppler vibrometry on a 3D-printed elastic ladder reveals boundary enhancement in a nearly flat band region, consistent with operation slightly below criticality. ZGV coalescence thus provides a bulk framework for in-band boundary resonances in reciprocal Hermitian lattices.

title: Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning for an Options Market Maker: An Empirical Study with Real S&P 500 Options
abstract: Options market makers absorb client order flow and must hedge the resulting inventory risk under trading frictions. We study whether an option hedging reinforcement learning (RL) agent trained on historical market data outperforms three alternatives in tail-risk protection: (i) traditional delta hedging, (ii) simple hedge-ratio rules, and (iii) the same agent trained in simulated markets. Most RL hedging agents are trained in model-generated markets that do not capture the crashes and volatility regimes present in real data. We introduce an empirical replay environment using S&P 500 option data from 1996 to 2017 and compare against a matched geometric Brownian motion (GBM) environment, a stochastic-volatility (SABR) simulator, and a hybrid that values historical paths with Black-Scholes, all sharing the same portfolio mechanics, stochastic arrivals, costs, and test period. We train a distributional Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) agent and evaluate it out of sample over 2018-2023. The agent trained on empirical data reduces Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) tail loss by 3.1% compared to delta hedging and outperforms every hedge-ratio rule chosen during the training period and every alternative training environment. The reduction reaches 8.9% in volatile and falling markets, but reverses to a cost of 7-10% in rising markets. Empirical training induces a state-dependent short net delta: the policy under-hedges negative-delta books, most strongly after prices have fallen. This tilt disappears with GBM training and is weaker with SABR or hybrid training. These findings suggest that exposure to historical market dynamics can materially change a tail-risk hedging policy, although the evidence rests on a single test path and the edge is regime-conditional.

title: Imaging spin entanglement with a scanning tunneling microscope
abstract: Artificial spin arrays assembled on surfaces enable atomic-scale studies of quantum correlations. Here we establish a hierarchy of connections between spin inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy (IETS) and entanglement in spin-$1/2$ systems. We first show that the number of spectroscopically active transitions in a spin-$1/2$ dimer serves as an entanglement witness. Using the leading-order tunneling conductance for the tip placed on spin $i$, $dI(i)/dV$, we then relate spectral moments $\mathcal{M}^{(n)}(i)=\int V^n(d^2I(i)/dV^2)\,dV$ to quantum correlations. The zeroth moment probes the one-tangle in systems with a gapped, nondegenerate ground state. For rotationally invariant Heisenberg systems, the first moment yields thermal spin correlators $\langle\boldsymbol S(i)\cdot\boldsymbol S(j)\rangle$, enabling reconstruction of nearest-neighbor concurrence and spatial imaging of entanglement in spin chains. It also provides access to the internal energy and magnetic specific heat, both usable as entanglement witnesses. Applying this approach to experimental IETS data from nanographene spin chains, we find good agreement with theory. We further discuss how the second moment probes longer-range correlations and the inverse moment relates to local spin susceptibility. For spin-$1/2$ trimers, we connect inter-multiplet inelastic spectral weight to genuine tripartite entanglement quantified by the concurrence fill. Finally, we reconcile the local character of IETS with its sensitivity to nonlocal entanglement through an analogy with digital quantum circuits, where Hamiltonian evolution implements multiqubit operations. These results establish IETS as a tool for quantifying and imaging entanglement in engineered on-surface spin systems.

title: Molecular Photoionization Spectra from Signed Dyson Orbitals and Anharmonic Nuclear Motion
abstract: Molecular photoelectron bands couple changes in nuclear structure to the energy-dependent scattering of the departing electron. Band intensities require both nuclear transition moments and electronic continuum amplitudes. We present SPARKS (Scattering and Photoionization: Amplitudes, Response Kernels and Spectra), a molecular photoionization approach that connects signed Dyson orbitals to complex molecular dipole amplitudes and harmonic or anharmonic nuclear transition moments. Compact B-spline and finite-element discrete-variable representations support spectral and sparse outgoing-boundary solvers. Independent molecular checks reproduce a reference H$_2^+$ spectrum and CO continuum amplitudes, while analytic hydrogen photoionization tests establish the continuum normalization. For H$_2$O/H$_2$O$^+$, electronic derivatives activate a Franck--Condon-dark fundamental and enter the same nuclear operator used in harmonic, perturbative and internal-coordinate variational calculations. Furan extends the nuclear treatment to all 21 vibrational coordinates in a selected configuration-interaction window, including low-lying out-of-plane states. Four epichlorohydrin ionization channels show how orbital mixing reshapes cross sections and angular distributions at similar Dyson norms. Energy conservation is imposed separately for every vibronic transition at fixed photon energy. The resulting spectra retain vibrational assignments and electronic interference, connecting weak-band activation, anharmonic spacings and photoelectron angular distributions within one physical description.

title: Deintercalation Equilibria Control the Composition, Structure, and Electronic Quality in the Synthesis of 2$M$-WS$_2$
abstract: Alkali-metal intercalation-deintercalation (AMID) enables access to metastable layered materials such as 2$M$-WS$_2$. Mechanistic studies of AMID have focused on intercalation; how deintercalation proceeds and influences crystal properties is comparatively poorly understood. Here, we assess 34 deintercalation treatments of 2$M$-K$_x$WS$_2$ and find that K$^+$ removal proceeds through coupled redox and ion-exchange equilibria, whose positions set the composition, structure, and electronic quality of the products. Across a series of neat solvents, K$^+$ deintercalation amount increased with solvent polarity and was driven to near-completion upon addition of nonoxidizing crown ether chelators, regardless of solvent polarity. Spontaneous reintercalation occurred when 2$M$-WS$_2$ was placed in dilute aqueous solutions of the strong base KOH but not the neutral salt KCl. These results suggest that the extent of deintercalation is governed by the stability of K$^+$ in solution, rather than oxidant strength alone, consistent with a reaction under thermodynamic control. Treatments that bias the deintercalation equilibrium most strongly toward the products while avoiding deleterious side reactions produce the highest quality 2$M$-WS$_2$. A six-hour treatment with acidified K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ gave the highest average residual resistivity ratio ($\overline{RRR}$). Residual K$^+$, quantified by ICP-MS, was found in all treated samples and appeared to impose an upper bound on $\overline{RRR}$. Treatments yielding crystals with $\overline{RRR}$ below this bound did not always afford 2$M$-WS$_2$; we observed two new structures in bleach-treated samples and signatures of alternative phases under other conditions. This work demonstrates that deintercalation is not merely a processing step in AMID but a mechanistically rich reaction that might be rationally tuned to improve and control metastable materials.

title: Bayesian transfer for offline Q-learning with multi-task Gaussian processes
abstract: Offline reinforcement learning can benefit from data collected in related tasks, yet indiscriminate knowledge transfer may lead to negative transfer under task mismatch and limited target-data coverage. We propose a target-aware Bayesian transfer framework for offline Q-learning based on multi-task Gaussian processes that jointly model task-specific Q-functions. Source tasks are assessed using target predictive evidence and maximum mean discrepancy (MMD), while posterior uncertainty and behavior-supported action sets guide conservative Bellman updates and policy extraction. To account for the dependence induced by Bellman bootstrapping, we distinguish Bellman innovations from bootstrap errors and establish stability and predictive source-selection results under explicit regularity conditions. We further derive selection-adaptive posterior contraction and offline policy-performance bounds, identifying the structural conditions under which source information can be pooled to achieve minimax-optimal rates in a shared-function Gaussian sequence experiment. Simulation studies with heterogeneous source tasks demonstrate improved target Q-function estimation and reduced material negative transfer compared with indiscriminate source pooling. An application to human decision-making data further shows higher average expected immediate payoff than both target-only learning and matched-size random source selection. These results highlight the benefits of combining target-aware source selection with uncertainty-aware conservative learning for reliable and sample-efficient offline reinforcement learning.
