title: Surface-Engineered BiVO4 Photocatalyst Enables Selective Water Oxidation for Water Splitting via a Photocatalysis–Electrolysis Hybrid System
abstract: Selective water oxidation in the presence of thermodynamically favored competing oxidation reactions remains a major challenge for photocatalytic systems. BiVO4 is one of the most efficient visible-light-responsive photocatalysts for water oxidation and exhibits high activity in Fe3+-mediated water-oxidation systems. However, although accumulated Fe2+ can introduce competing oxidation pathways under strongly acidic Fe3+/Fe2+ redox conditions, effective strategies for suppressing these processes and maintaining selective water oxidation remain largely unexplored.

title: Localized 4f Magnetism and Low-Lying 5d-Mediated Photoresponses in Layered TmI2
abstract: Divalent rare-earth solids with a 4fn+1 configuration provide access to electronic structures in which localized 4f states coexist with low-lying, structurally responsive 5d states, yet the combined magnetic, electrical, and optical manifestations of these states remain underexplored in extended Tm2+ compounds. Here, we investigate layered TmI2 as an extended Tm2+ solid and employ Cs4TmI6 with isolated TmI6 units and dilute SrI2:Tm2+ as targeted reference systems.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: AI for Postoperative Pain and Opioid Stewardship in Pediatric Surgery: A Systematic Review
abstract: ObjectivesTo synthesize evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled postoperative pain assessment and prediction, opioid-related risk prediction, patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) monitoring, and implementation considerations in pediatric surgical care.DesignA systematic review with narrative synthesis of evidence concerning AI applications in pediatric postoperative pain management and opioid stewardship.Data sourcesBiomedical, nursing, engineering, computer science, trial-registry, Google Scholar, and citation sources were systematically searched through March 2026.Review/analysis…
venue: Pain management nursing : official journal of the American Society of Pain Management Nurses

title: Electric Field Catalysis and the Metabolic Origin of Life
abstract: Metabolic theories for the origin of life postulate that chemical reaction networks emerged spontaneously from geochemistry and grew more complex due to positive feedback effects in catalysis. However, experimentally establishing protometabolic networks has proven challenging. In this Perspective, we make the case for electric field catalysis at charged aqueous interfaces as a crucial overlooked element for initiating protometabolic networks, an initial constraint that foreshadows the eventual takeover of electrostatic catalysis by enzymes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Cation-Effect-Driven Modulation of Interfacial Solvation Structures Enables Fast-Charging Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Fast battery charging is limited by sluggish Li+ transport at the anode/electrolyte interface, which is governed by the interfacial solvation structure (ISS). However, negative polarization disfavors anion accumulation at the anode interface, hindering the formation of anion-rich ISS required for rapid Li+ transfer. Here, leveraging the cation effect in electrocatalysis, we propose a cation-mediated strategy to reshape the interfacial electric field and construct anion-rich ISS in commercial electrolytes.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Exploring Chemical Concepts and Reactivity from Conceptual Density Functional Theory in Excited States via the ΔSCF Approach
abstract: Along with the recent development of the ΔSCF approach for excited state electronic structure description using density functional theory (DFT), we extend and develop conceptual density functional theory (CDFT) for evaluating chemical concepts and reactivity descriptors for both ground and excited states. Thereby, the fundamental energy functionalEJ[{npσ},v(r)] based on the generalized adiabatic connection Kohn–Sham (GAC-KS) theorem is introduced. Offering a straightforward interpretation of the reactivity of excited states analogous to that of the ground state.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Wafer-scale MoS2 and HZO-based Ferroelectric Field Effect Transistors with 4.4 V Memory Window for Back-End Compatible Multibit Memory
abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) with low-power operation and non-volatile data retention enabled by stable ferroelectric polarization switching, have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional floating-gate transistors for next-generation low-power memory applications. A FeFET with two-dimensional (2D) channel provides the opportunity for better electrostatic gate control and scalability beyond silicon. In this work, we report wafer scale 2D semiconductor-based FeFETs with Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 (HZO) gate stack showing unusual p-type charge transport and stable multibit memory properties. FeFETs based on 2-3 monolayer Molybdenum disulfide (MoS2) channel and a 20 nm HZO back gate oxide layer exhibit a large hysteresis with a memory window spanning 4.4 V under a operating voltage range of +3.8 to -3.8 V, and an ION/IOFF ratio of 10^5. We demonstrate that the polarization charge-induced modification of Schottky barrier width strongly affects the hole transport and memory properties of MoS2-HZO FeFETs. We further demonstrate several advantages and unique features of the FeFETs such as nondestructive data readout, non-volatile data retention under zero gate bias, low operation voltage, high write endurance and ultra-fast switching speed. These 1T memory cells can simplify the dense 3D integrated array architecture and offer additional practical functionalities, such as fast programming and erasing of large data arrays that are absent for many conventional memories. The demonstrated MoS2 and HZO-based FeFET shows great potential for on-chip complementary metal-oxide semiconductor (CMOS)-back-end-of-line (BEOL) compatible circuits for multifunctional devices, especially for 3D monolithically integrated architectures for AI workload.

title: Nucleophilicity from a Conceptual DFT Viewpoint: A Four-State Ensemble-Inspired Model
abstract: By taking advantage of the fundamental convexity of the exact energy as a function of the number of electrons, we extrapolate the straight-line segments connecting the N and N + 1 states and N – 2 and N – 1 states in a four-state ensemble-inspired model. These segments intersect at a unique point that determines a fractional charge transfer condition,ΔNint−=−λ, which naturally contemplates the reactivity of the cation and neutral forms in terms of their hardness.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
